correctness.rationale: Direct complex-polar substitution yields r_dot=r^7(-a+b cos4theta+c cos8theta), theta_dot=r^6(omega-b sin4theta-c sin8theta). Under omega>M angular speed never vanishes, and the exact full-turn logarithmic radius increment is I=J(a*-a). Differentiating log g eliminates b cos u+2c cos2u and leaves N=-cL. Pairing u and -u, expanding omega/(omega^2-X(u)^2), and using sin2u=2sin u cos u shows all surviving terms of L are nonpositive: A_{n,j}=(j-n)/(n+j+1) times a positive beta integral, 0<=j<=n, with n=1,j=0 strictly negative because b>0. This gives L<=-pi b^2/(2 omega^3), J<=2pi/(omega-M), and the quantitative bound. Polar time change dt/dtheta=(r^6g)^-1 makes successive-turn times a geometric series; sign I gives all three regimes, the t^-1/6 or (T-t)^-1/6 laws, and T=r0^-6 K/(1-exp(-6I)). The Poisson kernel at c=0 gives exact first slope q^2. Boundary omega=M is explicitly excluded. Independent adaptive quadrature at omega=1.8,b=.6,c=0,+/-.25,+/-.7 reproduced sign and lower bound (a*=+/-0.007522633 at |c|=.25, +/-0.024888029 at |c|=.7); numerical checks support but do not prove the universal sign.
